fine_trace.note: The first archive entry becomes the font bytes supplied by the input and drives the face selection path.
Additional archive entries are attached as metrics/auxiliary streams, carrying attacker-controlled AFM/PFM data into the Type 1 driver.

fine_trace.code: if ( clazz->attach_file ) error = clazz->attach_file( face, stream );
fine_trace.note: The generic attach API dispatches the attacker-controlled stream into the Type 1 attach_file implementation.

fine_trace.code: if ( fi->NumKernPair ) { t1_face->face_flags |= FT_FACE_FLAG_KERNING; face->afm_data = fi; fi = NULL; }
fine_trace.note: The metrics parser accepts the file and stores the parsed kerning table without validating that later glyph lookups will stay within the table bounds.

fine_trace.code: if ( face->afm_data ) T1_Get_Kerning( (AFM_FontInfo)face->afm_data, left_glyph, right_glyph, kerning );
fine_trace.note: The driver exposes the attached metrics object to kerning queries, forwarding the parsed table into the lookup routine.
Kerning lookup performs a binary search over the stored pair array and relies on the array bounds being valid.

fine_trace.code: if ( midi == idx ) { kerning->x = mid->x; kerning->y = mid->y; return; }
fine_trace.note: The lookup dereferences a kerning-pair element from the parsed table; if the table metadata is inconsistent, this read can step past the allocated array and trigger the heap-buffer-overflow.
